title: Quantifying Compound Retention in Drosophila melanogaster for Pharmacokinetic Studies
author: Sadova, Blank-Landeshammer, et al.

steps.title: Prepare larval cornmeal medium
steps.instruction: Weigh dry cornmeal medium ingredients (see Materials) into a 1 L beaker so that the final volume will be about half the beaker. Add water and stir without heating until no clumps remain. Tightly cover with aluminum foil and autoclave at 105 °C for 15 min (do not use a heating plate because the high viscosity can cause burns). Cool the autoclaved medium to 70 °C while stirring continuously. Add the propionic‑acid/methylparaben solution and stir well. Homogenize with an immersion blender if needed. Pour ~25–50 mL of medium into each stock bottle, cover with cheesecloth, let cool and solidify overnight. Store sealed at 2 °C–8 °C (up to 3 months).

steps.title: Prepare sugar‑yeast medium
steps.instruction: Weigh dry sugar‑yeast medium ingredients into a 1 L beaker. Add water and stir without heating until no clumps remain. Tightly cover with aluminum foil and place on a heating/stirring plate with a magnetic stir bar; bring to a boil. When agar foam climbs the beaker, remove from heat, discard the foil, and cool to 70 °C while stirring. Add propionic‑acid/methylparaben solution and stir well. Dispense ~25–50 mL per stock bottle or ~5 mL per narrow vial, cover with cheesecloth, let cool and solidify overnight. Store sealed at 2 °C–8 °C (up to 3 months).

steps.title: Prepare grape‑agar egg‑collection plates
steps.instruction: Add 500 mL water to a 1 L beaker, stir, then add powdered grape agar without heating until fully dissolved. Tightly cover with aluminum foil and bring to a boil; remove from heat, stir, and bring to a second boil as required by the manufacturer (Genesee Scientific, USA). Cool to ~60 °C while stirring, avoiding bubble formation. Pour ~6 mL into each sterile Petri dish, let solidify, cover with the dish lid, and store sealed upside‑down at 2 °C–8 °C.

steps.title: Generate age‑synchronized, sex‑sorted flies
steps.instruction: Set up a large‑scale culture to obtain synchronized F1 progeny, then collect, incubate, and sort flies for the CORE assay.

substeps.instruction: Mix 2 g active dry yeast with 4 mL water to a peanut‑butter consistency; place a smudge of this paste in the centre of a grape‑agar Petri dish.
Anesthetize 200–300 young male and female parental flies, transfer them into an egg cage, and top the cage with the yeast‑agar plate.
Keep the cage on its side until all flies awaken, then place it vertically in a climate chamber (25 °C, 60 % RH, 12:12 h light‑dark) so the plate is at the bottom. Leave for ~24 h.
Replace the agar plate the next day with a fresh one (no yeast paste) and leave for another 20–22 h (do not exceed 22 h, as eggs begin hatching after ~24 h at 25 °C).
Collect eggs from the agar plate using an ethanol‑cleaned paintbrush into a 15 mL tube, wash with DPBS until the supernatant is clear, then remove most liquid.

Dispense 40 µL of eggs into each stock bottle containing the larval cornmeal medium (use wide‑opening pipette tips or cut the first 2 cm off a 1 mL tip; release the plunger in one quick motion). Each bottle yields ~200–250 females and 150–200 males; adjust bottle number as needed for the experiment.
Incubate the stock bottles in the climate chamber for 10 days.
Transfer one‑day‑old eclosed flies to sugar‑yeast medium in stock bottles and allow them to mate for 2 days.
Sort age‑synchronized flies into groups of 30 males or 30 females.

Place the sex‑sorted flies on sugar‑yeast medium in narrow vials and cultivate until the desired experimental age (typically 5–7 days; if flies are older than 7 weeks, double the planned number to compensate for mortality).

steps.title: Prepare experimental CORE medium
steps.instruction: Make the dye‑containing, compound‑spiked agar medium, aliquot it into 0.5 mL tube caps, and solidify before the assay.

substeps.instruction: Gather ingredients as in Table 1 (example for 100 mL total): 5 g saccharose (5 %), 1.5 g agar‑agar (1.5 %), 0.48 mL propionic acid (0.48 %), 0.48 mL 10 % 4‑hydroxybenzoic acid methyl ester in ethanol (0.48 %), 0.2 g Brilliant Blue FCF (0.2 %), X % tested compound (e.g., 0.1 % powder = 0.1 g or 0.1 mL of a 10 % aqueous solution), deionized water to bring the total volume to ~100 mL (e.g., 98.52 mL water for the powder version, 97.52 mL for the solution version). Store the prepared medium at 2 °C–8 °C for no more than 1 week.
Prepare medium carriers: take 20–30 sterile 0.5 mL tubes per tested compound and place them open in a tube stand so that medium can be pipetted into the caps.

Prepare the medium matrix: weigh agar and saccharose into a dry 50 mL or 100 mL beaker, add deionized water, insert a magnetic stir bar, and stir well. Cover and bring to a boil, then cool to 70 °C or slightly below. Add propionic acid and the 4‑hydroxybenzoic acid methyl ester ethanolic solution, and keep the mixture on the stirring plate.

Prepare the compound of interest: if it is a powder, weigh the exact amount (weigh the paper before and after, and after transfer, to account for electrostatic loss; use an anti‑static gun or brush). If it is a solution of known concentration, proceed to the next step.
Prepare the reference dye: weigh the exact amount of Brilliant Blue FCF, recording the mass of the empty tray and the tray with dye; use anti‑static precautions as above.
Weigh the exact amount of the base medium (100 % minus the % of tested compound and dye) for each condition into 50 mL beakers.
Add the reference dye and the compound of interest to each beaker and stir vigorously to achieve a homogeneous suspension; ensure no material adheres to the beaker walls.

While the medium is still fluid, pipette it into the caps of the prepared 0.5 mL tubes (cut off the tip of a 1 mL pipette tip or use a wide‑opening tip). Pipette slightly above the cap level to compensate for shrinkage as the medium cools, but avoid spilling.
Let the medium cool and solidify for at least 1 hour before performing the CORE assay.

description: Drosophilamelanogaster (D. melanogaster, the fruit fly) is a well-recognized model organism for intestinal function research, as well as for the investigation of various bioactive molecules, such as artificial drugs and naturally occurring bioactive molecules. The protocol below describes the specific steps to apply D. melanogaster for the quantitation of the absorption, accumulation or excretion of the bioactive compounds, which were orally administered to a fruit fly.
